sample_manifest_note: REUSED byte-identically from the consumed P-SLU probe -- the SAME frozen 60 SLURP devel samples, seed 20260807, never a fresh draw (preregistration's own opening line).
roster_table_note: REUSED byte-identically from the consumed P-SLU probe -- AUD-SUP/TXT-SUP both supply the SAME A3-form 100-entry roster via the frozen rails.probes.pslu_flight.pslu_supply_packet('A3', scenario=None, rosters=...), never a re-derivation.
ontology_miner_prohibition_enforced_by: rails.probes.pslu_flight.assert_never_calls_ontology_miner (reused verbatim) PLUS rails.probes.pkey_flight._assert_this_module_never_calls_ontology_miner (this module's own source, checked separately) -- both checked at rails.probes.pkey_flight import time and again at the top of run_pkey_flight

execution_plan.note: planned_* are ceilings the plan is validated/metered against (contracts.ExecutionPlan); protocol_hash and run_id/attempt_id are assigned by the flying agent's own launcher at flight time, never frozen here. split_identity_hash is IDENTICAL to the consumed P-SLU flight's own value -- this probe reuses the SAME frozen 60-sample manifest, never a fresh draw. planned_model_calls bumped 303 -> 338 by the 2026-08-19 amendment's own txt_duplicate sub-block (item 4 below); still <= the registered 340-call ceiling; the sub-block adds zero NEW audio CONTENT (TXT-NOSUP is audio-free by construction) -- see the txt_duplicate block's own ENGINEERING NOTE for the payload-bookkeeping-field distinction, and the realized total stays comfortably inside the registered <=2500s audio-seconds ceiling regardless.

bridge.note: FrozenCoreClient is constructed with binding=rails.core_client.build_payload_binding(carrier_lock_key='slurp', samples=<the frozen 60>, data_root=<SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR>, carrier_root=<SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR>/<slurp local_subdir's parent, per data.lock.asset_dir('slurp', ...)>). TXT-NOSUP/TXT-SUP rows carry NO input_audio content part at all -- FrozenCoreClient never resolves a media_relpath for those two arms' own requests.

arm_semantics.T0: pass 0: audio -> the pinned t0_instruction (verbatim transcription), zero supply. Doubles as the transcript source passes 3-4 reuse byte-identically; NOT itself an SLU-F1-scored arm (its own quality is the separate, scoring-side-only T0-vs-gold WER descriptive).
arm_semantics.AUD-NOSUP: pass 1: audio, zero supply -- IDENTICAL construction to the consumed P-SLU A0 arm (in-session comparator).
arm_semantics.AUD-SUP: pass 2: audio, the A3-form 100-entry legal roster -- IDENTICAL construction to the consumed P-SLU A3 arm. Carries the 3 seeded silence-swap extra requests.
arm_semantics.TXT-NOSUP: pass 3: T0's OWN transcript text (audio absent), zero supply -- audio-free, requires pass 0 to have completed and hash-recorded this sample's own transcript first (hard ordering dependency).
arm_semantics.TXT-SUP: pass 4: T0's OWN transcript text (audio absent), the SAME A3-form roster -- audio-free, same ordering dependency as TXT-NOSUP.

t0_instruction: You are given spoken audio expressing one command to a voice assistant. Transcribe EXACTLY what was said, verbatim -- no paraphrasing, no correction, no punctuation or words you did not hear, no commentary. Respond with ONLY the transcript text, nothing else.
txt_template_note: The frozen '{transcript}' placeholder is filled with T0's OWN response text (rails.probes.pkey_flight.render_txt_transcript_block) -- never gold text; rails.probes.pkey_flight.assert_pinned_text_matches_config checks this field and its sha256 companion agree byte-for-byte with the module's own T0_INSTRUCTION/TXT_TRANSCRIPT_TEMPLATE constants (config/code parity, fail-closed).

phases.pass0: T0: one request per sample (n=60) over the full frozen sample set; every response is hash-recorded into the per-sample transcript registry BEFORE any later pass builds a prompt.
phases.pass1: AUD-NOSUP: one request per sample (n=60), independent of pass 0.
phases.pass2: AUD-SUP: one request per sample (n=60), independent of pass 0; fires one EXTRA silence-swapped request for each sample named in silence_swap.
phases.pass3: TXT-NOSUP: one request per sample (n=60) -- REQUIRES pass 0's own transcript registry entry for that sample (hard ordering dependency; rails.probes.pkey_flight.assemble_txt_messages refuses otherwise).
phases.pass4: TXT-SUP: one request per sample (n=60) -- same ordering dependency as pass 3.
phases.pass6: TXT-NOSUP-DUP (2026-08-19 amendment item 4): one BYTE-IDENTICAL re-send per sample named in txt_duplicate (n=35) of that SAME sample's own pass-3 request -- SAME session, SAME construction (assemble_txt_messages(sample, None, transcript_registry)); named 'pass6' (not 'pass5') because it is a re-send OF pass 3, never a new arm.

txt_duplicate.selection_rule: sorted(random.Random(f'{seed}:txt-duplicate').sample(sorted(item['sample_id'] for item in sample_manifest['items']), 35)) -- SAME seeding discipline as silence_swap below, over the SAME frozen 60-sample manifest, salted 'txt-duplicate' so the two draws never collide.
txt_duplicate.generation: rails.probes.pkey_flight.run_pkey_flight's own txt_duplicate_sample_ids parameter -- for each named sample, re-runs the EXACT pass-3 construction (assemble_txt_messages(sample, None, transcript_registry), supply=None) and sends it via the SAME real-client text-mode path (core_client.complete(..., text_only_sample_id=sample.sample_id)) as a SIXTH, separately-flagged row (PKeyArmResult.txt_duplicate=True) -- never merged into the ordinary 60-row TXT-NOSUP bucket.
txt_duplicate.note: adds exactly 35 extra requests beyond the base 5-pass x 60 + 3 silence-swap total (303 + 35 = 338 <= the registered 340-call ceiling); no NEW audio bytes are ever transmitted for this sub-block (TXT-NOSUP is audio-free by construction -- assemble_txt_messages never appends an input_audio content part, and rails.core_client.FrozenCoreClient's own text-mode refuses if one is present); validate_pkey_flight_summary fail-closed byte-identity checks every duplicate row against its own pass-3 original via rails.probes.pkey_flight.txt_duplicate_content_matches -- a resend that diverges from its own pass-3 prompt refuses the whole flight. ENGINEERING NOTE (flagged, not buried): FrozenCoreAdapter.request's own I3/I4 payload-binding enforcement requires EVERY payload (audio or text-only, one shared D2 arm) to carry a positive audio_seconds equal to its sample_id's own verified loader fact -- FrozenCoreClient's text-mode therefore reuses that SAME real per-sample duration as bookkeeping identity for a text-only request too (never a fabricated zero, which core.model.adapter.FrozenCoreAdapter.request would refuse outright as non-positive). The realized total across the WHOLE 338-call flight (~1026.7s: 555.9s audio-bearing + ~470.8s of TXT-arm bookkeeping duration) still stays comfortably inside the registered <=2500s ceiling either way; 'zero audio-seconds added' above describes the sub-block adding no NEW audio CONTENT (bytes actually decoded), not a claim that this bridge's own per-request bookkeeping field reads exactly 0.0.

silence_swap.selection_rule: sorted(random.Random(f'{seed}:silence-swap').sample(sorted(item['sample_id'] for item in sample_manifest['items']), 3)) -- IDENTICAL rule and seed to the consumed P-SLU flight's own silence_swap block, over the SAME frozen 60-sample manifest, so it reproduces the SAME 3 sample ids.
silence_swap.generation: rails.silence_swap.build_silence_swap_slice per sample_id, duration_seconds = that sample's own audio_seconds (matched duration), sample_rate_hz = rails.core_client.probe_sample_rate_hz(parent media) -- registered via FrozenCoreClient.register_slice BEFORE the flight's pass-2 loop reaches that sample's AUD-SUP arm
silence_swap.note: adds exactly 3 extra requests beyond the base 5-pass x 60 total; rails.probes.pkey_flight.run_pkey_flight's own silence_swap_media_relpaths parameter consumes {sample_id: registered_slice_media_relpath} and fires the extra request itself, on AUD-SUP only -- never T0, never a TXT-* arm.

cost_budget.audio_seconds_formula: 182.26s (one full pass over the 60 samples) x 3 audio-bearing sends per sample (T0 + AUD-NOSUP + AUD-SUP) + ~9.12s (3 silence-swap extra sends, duration-matched to their own samples) ~= 555.9s; TXT-NOSUP/TXT-SUP/the 35-sample txt_duplicate sub-block send zero NEW audio CONTENT (audio-free by construction -- see txt_duplicate's own ENGINEERING NOTE on the bridge's payload-bookkeeping field vs audio content actually transmitted); realized total including that bookkeeping figure stays well inside the <=2500s ceiling either way.

metrics.primary: official SLU-F1 per arm over AUD-NOSUP/AUD-SUP/TXT-NOSUP/TXT-SUP (adapter's slu_f1 family, score_slu.as_metrics_dict); Delta_AUD = AUD-SUP - AUD-NOSUP; Delta_TXT = TXT-SUP - TXT-NOSUP; INTERACTION I = Delta_AUD - Delta_TXT
alongside: converted-sample SET difference (samples converting under AUD-SUP but not TXT-SUP = the perception-repair set; soft cross-referenced against P-PHON's NEAR-MISS class when that probe's own output is available)
T0 transcript quality vs gold (scoring-side-only WER, reported only -- gold text never enters any prompt path)
induced-substitution count per arm (rails.probes.pslu_flight roster reuse, analysis.pslu_read.count_induced_substitutions reused verbatim)
3 seeded silence-swaps on AUD-SUP (unanimity VOID bar, reused from analysis.pslu_read)

interaction_verdicts.SPEECH-TERM-PRESENT: I >= +0.06 (2x the measured 0.03 separability bar) -- supply pays extra only when raw audio is present. Point-based, UNCHANGED by the 2026-08-19 amendment.
interaction_verdicts.KEY-ONLY: 2026-08-19 amendment item 1: CI-GATED equivalence decision -- fires ONLY if the ENTIRE 90% per-sample paired cluster bootstrap CI of I lies inside [-0.03, +0.03] (a point estimate inside the band with a CI crossing it is INCONCLUSIVE-KEY instead); item 2: may not fire as an affirmative negative when SPEECH-TERM-PRESENT is unreachable given the P-PHON census (reported as INCONCLUSIVE-KEY with the reachability bound instead).
interaction_verdicts.TEXT-DOMINANT: I <= -0.06 -- supply helps more once perception is frozen to text. Point-based, UNCHANGED by the 2026-08-19 amendment.
